questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country the university was situated in, the courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, i believe I got most of my information via mail or the UNIBO website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: If i got any, it was through mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing at first, but they were just a bit late with their orientation mail and so on.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find housing. I had to go to Bologna a few months before my mobility to find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Write to previous students, most likely they will know some local landlords who they can recommend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is not impossible to find housing, but start as early as possible to search for housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The first week or so, students can browse through the different courses  and visit different courses. After that, they can simply follow them. 

Students have to be checked in however, to make sure that they are actually registered for the courses. This is quite a difficult process, as you have to do it manually online. They only check in about 60 people per day, meaning that you have to be patient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UNIBO website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes i wanted. There was some problems however, as my professor changed the time of one my classes two times. It all got sorted in the end however.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Browse some of the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were about the same level as the danish courses. Others were quite a lot easier however. Overall it was just a bit different.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The exams were very different and were generally more focused on memorization and in-person exams, rather than 10 and 72 hour exams. There was also a bigger focus on discussions rather than analyses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
96338 - POLITICAL BEHAVIOR AND INSTITUTIONS - for DAK3

91143 - Politics And Policies In The European Union - for EP

90450 - China In Africa - elective

88911 - Visualizing The Italian Society - elective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Especially the China in Africa course, as i really liked getting an insight into China's influence on the African continent.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did sports, were i had to get a sports certificate in order to play volleyball.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and drinks were generally cheaper, most groceries were as well. 
Public transport were cheaper as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most activities were available such as sports, events, trips and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played volleyball at a local Italian volleyball team. I would highly recommend that, as i got to interact with the locals and practice my Italian.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see other cities, and travel around as much as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. Just get used to people blowing their nose just about anywhere.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any, really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid back style of life

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not stress about registering for courses, checking in and so on. The problems will get solved over time.

Join a local club/sport and interact with the locals. 

Make sure to find housing as soon as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live in another country, and exploring a different style of life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing, getting my pre-approval for the courses to get merit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
